---
title: "Version 4: assembling a cross-study cohort"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

# Overview

Starting with version 4.0.0, `curatedMetagenomicData` reads profiles from the
public curatedMetagenomicData releases at
<https://cmgd-public.cancerdatasci.org> through the
[cmgdr](https://github.com/seandavi/cmgdr) package, instead of from
ExperimentHub. The user-facing functions `curatedMetagenomicData()`,
`returnSamples()` and `mergeData()` keep their signatures and return types.

Three things changed underneath them.

1. **Releases.** A dataset is one registration of the
   [curatedMetagenomicsNextflow](https://github.com/seandavi/curatedMetagenomicsNextflow)
   pipeline, and a release is an immutable snapshot of it named by its build
   date. Each version of this package pins one; `cmdRelease()` shows which.
2. **Sample identity.** Samples are keyed by the release's `sample_key`.
   Curated metadata is joined to the release by run accession.
3. **Metadata columns.** `sampleMetadata` keeps its name and takes the cMD 4
   data dictionary columns.

This article walks through the cross-study workflow: filter the curated
metadata, call `returnSamples()`, and work with what comes back.

# Packages

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(curatedMetagenomicData)
library(dplyr)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
```

# The release in use

```{r}
cmdRelease()
```

A release holds the studies the pipeline has processed so far. Studies named
by a BioProject accession are processed but not yet curated.

```{r}
cmgdr::cmgd_studies(cmdRelease()) |> head(10)
```

To read a different release, set the options before any data-access call. The
published datasets and releases are listed by `cmgdr::cmgd_datasets()` and
`cmgdr::cmgd_releases()`.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
options(curatedMetagenomicData.release = "latest")
```

# The curated metadata

`sampleMetadata` has one row per curated sample. The columns of the cMD 4
data dictionary are named in its `harmonized` attribute; the rest are the
ontology term ids for those fields and study-specific columns that have not
yet been harmonized. It is built from
`curatedMetagenomicDataCuration::makeCombinedMetadata()` by
`data-raw/sampleMetadata.R`, so the package does not depend on the curation
repository at run time.

```{r}
dim(sampleMetadata)
head(attr(sampleMetadata, "harmonized"), 12)
```

Not every curated sample is in the release yet, and not every sample in the
release is curated. `returnSamples()` reports what it drops.

# Define a cohort

Adult stool samples from two studies that are in the release:

```{r}
cohort <- sampleMetadata |>
    filter(
        study_name %in% c("AsnicarF_2017", "ZellerG_2014"),
        body_site == "feces",
        age_years >= 18
    ) |>
    select(where(~ !all(is.na(.x))))

count(cohort, study_name)
```

# Return the profiles

```{r}
tse <- returnSamples(cohort, "relative_abundance", rownames = "short")
tse
```

The columns are named by `sample_key`. The `colData` holds the cohort's
columns followed by the release's per-sample QC columns: `sample_key`,
`run_ids`, the read counts, `number_reads` (reads after host decontamination,
which `counts = TRUE` multiplies by), the MetaPhlAn index and the pipeline
version and commit.

```{r}
colData(tse)[1:3, c("study_name", "sample_id", "sample_key", "number_reads", "metaphlan_index")]
```

The `rowData` holds the seven ranks parsed from the MetaPhlAn clade string and
the integer `ncbi_taxid`. MetaPhlAn 4 species-level genome bins without a
named species have no identifier.

```{r}
rowData(tse) |> head(3)
mean(is.na(rowData(tse)$ncbi_taxid))
```

# Other data types

`marker_abundance` and `marker_presence` are read from the release catalog
rather than per-study files, so they take longer (about 15 seconds per
study). `bracken` and `resistome` are new in version 4.

```{r}
resistome <- returnSamples(cohort, "resistome")
resistome
head(rownames(resistome), 3)
```
